Overview.Description: BedRock verifies video authenticity by recomputing a rolling SHA-256 hash chain over fixed-size video segments, then comparing the resulting trail against immutable HashRecorded events stored in a per-video Subcontract on the Stability blockchain. Any modification to any byte of the original recording is detectable down to the 1.25 MB segment level.

Phase.name: SegmentHashing
Phase.Title: Hash Video Buffer into Segment Digests
Phase.Description: The raw video file buffer is divided into fixed-size segments. Each segment is zero-padded to exactly SEG_SIZE bytes before hashing, ensuring identical output regardless of whether the segment is a full chunk or the final short-tail chunk.

Step.Action: Receive raw video file buffer (ArrayBuffer / Buffer)
Step.Detail: Accepted via multipart upload at POST /api/verify or loaded from disk in the offline rehash tool.

Step.Action: Iterate over the buffer in SEG_SIZE-byte windows
Step.Pseudocode: for i in 0 .. ceil(fileSize / SEG_SIZE) - 1: chunk = buffer[ i*SEG_SIZE : (i+1)*SEG_SIZE ]

Step.Action: Zero-pad each chunk to exactly SEG_SIZE bytes
Step.Pseudocode: paddedChunk = new Uint8Array(SEG_SIZE) // all zeros paddedChunk.set(chunk) // overwrite leading bytes
Step.Detail: Zero-padding mirrors the frontend recording logic, which always writes fixed-size typed arrays to disk. Without padding, a truncated final segment would hash differently between environments.

Step.Action: Compute segHash_i = SHA-256(paddedChunk)
Step.Detail: Produces a 32-byte (256-bit) digest. Environment-specific implementations produce identical byte output: - Backend (Node.js): node:crypto createHash('sha256') - Frontend (browser): crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", ...) - Offline tool (Python): hashlib.sha256

Phase.name: RollingHashChain
Phase.Title: Recalculate Rolling Hash Chain and Derive Final Hash
Phase.Description: Segment digests are chained together via successive SHA-256 hashes to produce a tamper-evident rolling hash trail. Each entry in the trail accumulates all prior video content; any modification at segment i cascades forward and corrupts every subsequent rolling hash.

Step.Action: Compute genesis rolling hash (segment 0)
Step.Detail: The genesis value is a double-hash of the first segment's digest. It serves as the video's unique on-chain identity key (see Phase 3).

Step.Action: Compute rolling hash for each subsequent segment i ≥ 1
Step.Pseudocode: for i in 1 .. numSegments - 1: roll_i = SHA-256( roll_{i-1} || segHash_i )
Step.Detail: || denotes byte-level concatenation of the two 32-byte digests, yielding a 64-byte input to SHA-256.

Step.Action: Store full rolling hash trail as array of records
Step.Pseudocode: trail[i] = { index: i, segHashHex: hex(segHash_i), rollingHex: hex(roll_i) }

Step.Action: Extract finalRollingHex from last record

Phase.name: OnChainLookup
Phase.Title: Search Blockchain for Subcontract Address Using First Hash
Phase.Description: The genesis rolling hash (roll_0) acts as a globally unique identity key. The Grandfather smart contract maintains a registry mapping each video's identity hash to the address of its per-video Subcontract. This phase locates the correct Subcontract without the caller needing to supply it.

Step.Action: Extract firstHash from the rolling hash trail
Step.Pseudocode: firstHash = trail[0].rollingHex // == roll_0 from Phase 2 firstHashBytes32 = "0x" + firstHash
Step.Detail: Called via computeFirstHash(fileBuffer) which internally calls hashVideoBuffer() and returns records[0].rollingHex.

Step.Action: Determine Subcontract address resolution path

Case.condition: subcontractAddress provided by caller in request body
Case.Action: Validate address is a well-formed 20-byte hex string
Use provided address directly; skip on-chain lookup
Proceed to on-chain lookup using firstHashBytes32

Step.Action: Query Grandfather contract on Stability blockchain
Step.Detail: The Grandfather contract is the factory and registry for all Subcontracts. It stores a mapping: bytes32 firstHash => address subcontract. Lookup is a read-only eth_call; no gas is required.

Step.Action: Evaluate lookup result

Case.Action: Return null; trigger END STATE 3 — NOT FOUND

Case.condition: returned address is a valid non-zero address
Case.Action: Store as resolvedSubcontractAddress; proceed to Phase 4

Phase.name: OnChainHashTrail
Phase.Title: Retrieve On-Chain Rolling Hash Trail from Subcontract
Phase.Description: With the Subcontract address resolved, the backend reads the contract state and scrapes all HashRecorded events emitted during the original recording session. These events constitute the immutable on-chain hash trail against which the locally recalculated trail is compared.

Step.Action: Authorize Subcontract as a legitimate child of Grandfather
Step.Pseudocode: authorized = grandfather.isAuthorizedChild(resolvedSubcontractAddress) if not authorized: throw UnauthorizedSubcontractError
Step.Detail: Prevents forged or externally deployed contracts from spoofing verification results.

Step.Action: Read Subcontract state variables in parallel
Scrape all HashRecorded events from Subcontract
Step.Pseudocode: events = [] for blockRange in chunks(deploymentBlock, latestBlock, chunkSize=25000): events += subcontract.queryFilter("HashRecorded", blockRange) events.sortBy(e => e.args.sequence)

Field.name: newHash
Field.label: Rolling hash submitted at this sequence

Step.Action: Retry if event count is less than totalEntries

RetryPolicy.Reason: RPC log indexing lag on the Stability network

Step.Action: Extract on-chain final hash from last sorted event

Phase.name: Comparison
Phase.Title: Compare Calculated Trail Against On-Chain Trail
Phase.Description: Each element of the locally recalculated rolling hash trail is compared against the corresponding on-chain HashRecorded event. A full match produces VERIFIED. Any mismatch or length discrepancy produces TAMPERED, with precise segment-level forensic information.

Step.Action: Normalize both hash values for comparison
Compare trail lengths
Compare rolling hashes position-by-position
No divergence found — all hashes match

EndState.name: VERIFIED
EndState.Title: Video is Authentic
EndState.TriggerCondition: Every calculatedTrail[i].rollingHex matches onChainTrail[i].newHash for all i, AND both trails have equal length.

UIPresentation.Detail: Hash trail accordion with per-segment match summary and Subcontract details.

EndState.name: TAMPERED
EndState.Title: Video Has Been Modified
EndState.TriggerCondition: At least one calculatedTrail[i].rollingHex does NOT match onChainTrail[i].newHash, OR the two trails have different lengths.

Field.name: divergenceSegmentIndex
Field.label: Zero-based index of first modified segment

Field.name: segmentStartSecond
Field.label: Start of tampered segment in seconds

Field.name: segmentEndSecond
Field.label: End of tampered segment in seconds

Field.name: calculatedHash
Field.label: What we computed at divergence index

Field.name: onChainHash
Field.label: What was recorded on-chain at divergence index

UIPresentation.Detail: Segment timeline visualization: matching segments shown green, divergent segment shown red, all subsequent segments shown faded-red (cascade-affected). Clickable tampered-segment card seeks video playback to segmentStartSecond and auto-pauses at segmentEndSecond.

EndState.CascadeNote: Because each rolling hash chains into the next, a modification at segment i invalidates all segments i+1 through N. The UI distinguishes the first true divergence from cascade failures to pinpoint the actual tamper location.

EndState.name: NOT_FOUND
EndState.Title: No Blockchain Record Found / Verification Error
EndState.TriggerCondition: EITHER: Grandfather.getSubcontractByFirstHash(firstHash) returns the zero address (video identity hash not registered on-chain). OR: A runtime error occurred — unauthorized subcontract, network failure, malformed address, or unrecoverable RPC error.

Field.name: hint
Field.label: Present only for lookup-failure case; absent for generic errors

SubCase.Detail: Explains two likely causes: (a) The video's first segment was modified, changing its identity hash and making it unresolvable against the original on-chain registration. (b) The recording is still being written to the blockchain (write lag).
Displays the error message string from the response payload.

FlowSequence.Step: Ingest raw video buffer from upload or disk.
Slice buffer into SEG_SIZE chunks; zero-pad each to SEG_SIZE.
Compute segHash_i = SHA-256(paddedChunk_i) for each segment.
Build rolling hash chain: roll_0 = SHA-256(segHash_0); roll_i = SHA-256(roll_{i-1} || segHash_i).
Extract firstHash = roll_0 (identity key) and calculatedFinalHash = roll_{N-1}.
Query Grandfather contract on-chain: getSubcontractByFirstHash(firstHash) → subcontractAddress.
If zero address returned → END STATE 3 (NOT FOUND).
Authorize subcontract as a legitimate child of Grandfather.
Scrape all HashRecorded events from deploymentBlock to latestBlock in 25,000-block chunks; retry up to 10× on count mismatch.
Sort events by sequence; extract onChainFinalHash = last event's newHash.
Compare calculatedTrail against onChain event trail position-by-position.
First mismatch at index i → compute forensic metadata → END STATE 2 (TAMPERED).
